done.why: I ate the shrinking cake in the tea room without bringing another cake along, so I ended up tiny in the Posts Room with chasms on both sides and the cakes out of reach on the table. The only thing left to try was the pool. I swam in it, drowned, and woke up back at the barrow without any of my things. That was over 260 turns in, and after so much fighting with the spinning room I didn't have it in me to walk all the way back and pick everything up again.

about: You're a treasure hunter under the ground in the old Empire. A cranky Wizard took the Empire's treasures and hid them south of a ravine, and he keeps appearing to throw half-finished spells at you (float, freeze, a fake copy of a book). It's a big puzzle-box of a place. You answer a riddle carved over a door, float up a well in a bucket by pouring water into it, get a key out from behind a locked door with a place mat, and order a tin robot around to stop a spinning room and lift a cage off you. It's funny and a bit tongue-in-cheek, and the places feel like somebody built them a long time ago and then left.

ending.what: I died once, drowning in the pool of tears, and was brought back by a big face in the mist that called me a 'wanderer' and sent me back to the barrow. That isn't an ending, though.

moments.note: I asked out loud why the lantern was familiar and got 'That sentence isn't one I recognize.' So it doesn't take questions.
'take the sword too' gave me 'You can't see any such thing' when the sword was right in front of me. The word 'too' broke it.
'walk into the tunnel' got me told to use compass directions. Fair enough, but I'd never have guessed that.
The Wizard's first appearance is great. He sizes me up and pretty much tells me where to go: pearls behind a stone door that asks a question, past a room that won't keep still.
The copy of ZORK I vanished when I reached for it, and the room 'settles down and is only a room.' I worked out that the Wizard's 'Fantasize!' spell had made it up. Clever.
I tried to pet the unicorn and it decided I was an 'uncouth sort of vagabond' and melted into the hedges.
Looking at the unicorn showed the key on its ribbon, and the text gently told me it isn't meant for me: 'It will wait for her. You need not.'
The spinning room threw me out somewhere random, then explained itself: the floor is turning and somebody could stop it. That gave me a goal.
'go back south' wasn't understood.
I pushed the letter opener into the keyhole and heard a little noise and saw dust behind the door. Then I pulled the place mat back and the key was on it. Very satisfying.
'take the key and unlock the door' picked up the key and then said I needed 'the right one.' I had to say 'iron key'.
Spent ages going in and out of the Carousel Room and landing somewhere random every time, trying to find the riddle door.
I just typed 'a well' as my answer and it worked: a clap of thunder and the stone door swung open.
The Wizard made me float right outside the Pearl Room, so I couldn't move for ages and kept getting 'flapping your arms?'. Waiting it out took about a dozen turns.
Pouring the teapot into the bucket sent me up the well. 'Well done.' Made me laugh.
Asked about a robot I hadn't met and got told it was waiting in the Low Room and that 'An order carries about as far as your voice does.' Handy, if a bit spoiler-y.
Frozen solid by the Wizard. More turns lost just waiting.
The cage dropped and gas started coming in, and the robot was in there with me. I told it to lift the cage, it threw it across the room, and 'the robot appears to be smiling.'
Poison gas was filling the room and I got 'You're holding too many things already!' I had to drop something in a panic.
The bit about the spinning compass: 'What compass, you ask? The one which allows you to specify compass directions for movement.'
Shrunk and stuck. Nothing warned me I'd need a second cake to get big again, and nothing I tried in the Posts Room got me out.
Drowned in the pool, and a huge face that's locked up somewhere sent me back, hinting that I owe it a favour now. Interesting, but all my things were gone.

wished: To ask questions in plain sentences, like 'why is the lantern familiar?' or 'what did fantasize do to me?', and get some kind of answer instead of 'That sentence isn't one I recognize.'
To say 'go back' or 'walk into the tunnel' without having to know compass directions.
Some warning before eating the cake that I'd need to take another one with me, or some way back up to the table once I was small.
Some way to choose where I come out of the Carousel Room before stopping it, because so many turns went on random exits.
To keep my things after dying, or at least be told where they ended up.

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you; the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question, and the rest further in, past a room that will not keep still.
lines.why: A hint that reads like part of the story. It kept me going for the whole first half.

lines.line: The room, which had been looking a little odd round the edges, settles down and is only a room.
lines.why: This is how I found out the ZORK book was something the Wizard made up. Quiet and creepy.

lines.line: It will wait for her. You need not.
lines.why: A polite way of telling me to leave the key alone. It worked on me.

lines.line: A thing that is turned can presumably be stopped, by somebody who finds the works.
lines.why: It made the annoying spinning room into a puzzle I could actually solve.

lines.line: You are at the top of the well. Well done.
lines.why: A pun at the moment I'd earned it.

lines.line: The cage shakes and is hurled across the room. It's hard to say, but the robot appears to be smiling.
lines.why: The robot became a friend at that moment.

lines.line: What compass, you ask? The one which allows you to specify compass directions for movement.
lines.why: It jokes about the very rule that had been confusing me since turn 7.

fun.why: When a puzzle clicked it felt great: the key and the place mat, the riddle, the bucket, the robot and the cage. A lot of turns in between went on the random spinning room and waiting out the Wizard's spells.

engagement.why: The Wizard's hint and the little explanations, like the floor turning and the robot not being able to hear me, always gave me something to aim for. I only lost heart once I was shrunk, stuck, drowned and stripped of everything.

difficulty.why: For someone new to this, the spinning room and the cake trap were harsh. I could make myself stuck with no way out and nothing warned me. The parser also wanted particular wording ('iron key', no 'too', no 'go back').

interestingness.why: The made-up book that disappears, the Wizard's half-finished spells, the robot obeying orders and the mysterious face after I died all made the place feel alive and a bit mischievous.

prose.why: The writing is dry and funny all the way through: the uncouth vagabond, the robot smiling, 'Well done', the compass joke. The added lines, like the unicorn's ribbon and the turning floor, are gentle and well judged.
